source_and_lifecycle_findings.evidence: candidateAssetVisible requires loaded status, visible ancestors through the exact scene, non-disposed record and WeakMap verification receipt matching model ID, active web/lod variant, file, SHA256 and byte count. GLB extras alone cannot activate clipping.

View changes abort ordinary fetches, retainDetailResult rejects obsolete results, load finally resynchronizes visibility, and hidden candidates clear clips/collisions. Failed upgrades retain only the previously verified visible variant.

Each clip triangle carries macro hash and feature_local_id. Broadway has both confirmed render parts, 3245 and 3246. Candidate hooks are released before CityFeatureMask rebind and reapplied afterward; original hooks are restored on disposal.

Near GLBs lack per-feature IDs, so masking is bounded by registered source-intersection polygons and source macro. The eight identified urban buildings use source intersections; unresolved Song and Lu Xun owners have null replacement geometry. This is a display correction, not survey accuracy.

Overture clipping requires exact source IDs; remaining geometry is polygon difference with original properties retained. OSM corrections remain limited to the same bounded geographic polygons. Unrelated IDs, geometry errors and conflicting property groups retain source geometry.

OSMBuildingSuppressor restores original IDs before replacement, waits for residual readiness, uses source epochs/generations to reject late plans, and retains originals on query/upload failure. Failed removal retains the previous residual until restoration succeeds.

Actual merge keeps all original 40 records deeply equal and produces 70 unique IDs. All 30 additions are overview-only. Candidate catalogue fetch/validation errors fall back to existing records. Provider fallback synchronously refreshes candidate vector controllers.

observations: Anchor and label GeoJSON retain all 70 IDs and full names without model fetch/LOD dependency or clustering.
Layer minzoom is zero and maxzoom is omitted; actual vendored style validation accepts the layers and zoom 24.
Dense cards use stable model numbers and 24 by 20 pixel sprites; full-name and compact layers have complementary filters.
Layout reserves actual sidebar, tool strip, legend and location-card rectangles; tested at desktop, 390 by 844 and 320 by 568.

Current screen-card rectangles resolve the topmost model first; only a miss queries the unchanged original-lamp layer. Click and hover share this path, stale label query boxes are ignored, and duplicate original events are suppressed. All owned listeners, layers, sources and DOM elements are released on destroy.
Labels keep their true geographic coordinates and use viewport text/icon offsets. A sky slot never unprojects into a false geographic label; its optional leader becomes zero length.

GeoJSON properties contain scalars only. Pixel vectors now live in match-by-ID style expressions with literal vec2 outputs, preventing GeoJSON-vt array-to-string conversion. Unknown IDs fall back to [0,0]; the actual vendor style validator accepts the generated layers.

Both label layers require inViewport and retain complementary compact filters. Their GeoJSON still carries every model ID; the original 70 anchor layer has no viewport filter or zoom-dependent visibility change. Labels return when their anchor returns to the viewport.

On the shortest phone layout, compact grids retry with zero inter-card gap only when the 2px-gap grid is insufficient. The sprite transparent border remains; card size, text size and hit rectangles are unchanged. The 243x158 available area now fits 10x7 cards.

observations: GLB coordinates transform as east=cos(h)*x-sin(h)*z and north=-sin(h)*x-cos(h)*z, matching the scene group rotationY=-heading and latitude scaling.

observations: A memory-budget failure before far rebinding disposes only the newly allocated mask, preserving the existing candidate material hook and shadow materials.

Once rebinding begins, catch first releases the candidate wrapper, disposes the failed CityFeatureMask, and clears parent.mask only when it refers to that failed mask. Retry therefore allocates a fresh live mask.

Candidate hooks are restored only when the streamer is not destroyed, the same parent remains registered for the object, the same index controller is current, and the far object remains attached through its ancestor chain to this scene.

Failure after prepared records are registered removes precisely those records from wanted and global records, clears the parent record list only when still identical, and aborts a partially started matching near request. Existing loader abort/wanted/parent checks discard a late parse result.
Objects removed from the scene, detached from the parent registry or belonging to a destroyed streamer do not regain hooks. CityFeatureMask disposal is idempotent in those paths.
prepareFarObject still releases candidate hooks, disposes its mask, removes its parent record and throws. It does not restore clipping on a failed object the upstream loader discards.

Tests use actual Three.js materials and invoke production shader hooks for standard, depth and distanceRGBA passes, checking current clip uniforms, absence of disposed-mask uniforms, nonduplicated wrappers and clean retry.
post_browser_failure_recovery_review.conclusion: No remaining blocking issue found in this bounded post-browser error-path delta.
